Preface

Huynh Hiep is a young Vietnamese pharmacist, currently living in Sacramento, California State Capital, USA, and is a lay disciple of the late Venerable Master Tuyen Hoa at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. I always have a wish towards Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva as well as wanting to establish a Ksitigarbha project to help those who have an affinity with Him through books or images.

At the end of 2007, when I was in retreat for the 5th time in Australia, Huynh Hiep asked me to translate the Japanese version into Vietnamese of the spiritual stories of Ksitigarbha without the head in Fuchu, Hiroshima. So I started working again and over 4 months, the translation was completed in the United States in April 2008 with nearly 900 typewritten pages, divided into 3 volumes. At first, I only posted it on the website quangduc.com in Australia and viengiac.de in Germany, but many people wanted to read the book, so Huynh Hiep once again lobbied the Taiwan Tinh Tong Hoc Association in the US to have this book published in Taiwan. In October 2010, the Buddha-Education Kim Hoi of the Tinh Tong Hoc Association in Taiwan published 1,500 copies. Each set has 3 books, until now (2012) there are no more sets left. Therefore, Vietnamese Buddhists in Southern and Northern California in the United States want to republish the first edition and I have also written a preface for this republishing. Now, Huynh Hiep wants me to edit the book "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Record of Inspiration", the Chinese version translated by Mr. Lieu Nguyen and I also started working during this 2012 Summer Retreat season.He is Chinese, his Chinese is very good, but in Vietnamese, the ideas and lyrics need to be completely revised. But thanks to this, I learned many more stories of inspiration and cause and effect through the manifestation of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in China from the Tang Dynasty until now. This is truly a rare and wonderful thing.

Although Dao Huu Dieu Hai in Canada tried to type according to Mr. Lieu Nguyen's translation, there are still many places where the meaning and words are still unclear. Therefore, I asked Venerable Thich Nu Chon Toan to review everything and type in any errors. It is true that the Nun also has a predestined relationship with Ksitigarbha. Four years ago, she also helped type the book about Ksitigarbha that I translated from Japanese into Vietnamese. Now Huynh Hiep wants me to write a preface for this book, in order to record the timeline as well as the translation and recording work of the ancients, leaving it for future generations and Huynh Hiep will also ask the Tinh Tong Hoc Association in Taiwan to publish it, helping Vietnamese people in all five continents have the opportunity to read the cause and effect stories and manifestations of Lord Ksitigarbha in this book to practice and to avoid evil and do good. I of course did not refuse, because this was something worth doing. Therefore, I took the pen to write these words to leave behind for future generations. In addition, Teacher Hanh Ly also helped correct spelling errors for the final time and Dao Huu Nhu Than arranged the layout of this book. Thank you very much.

The Record of Premonition Luc

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, making a profound vow, has long proven the same dharma, but has not returned to the light, has not attained Buddhahood, with great compassion, he spreads throughout the world, manifests according to his type, and saves sentient beings, as always in the dark places. To save sentient beings suffering in hell, using the Bodhisattva of the past to increase, make a great vow, to save sentient beings to attain Bodhi, and if the hell is not yet clean, they will not become Buddha. The nature of sentient beings is inherently good and is no different from Buddha's. Because of confusion, they are deluded and delusional in the real world. Should arise greed, anger, ignorance, create killing, religion, lust, so reincarnation in the six paths cannot escape, there is no time to escape. There are few people who are born in heaven, but many who fall into the three realms. The Bodhisattva takes pity and helps many species, hoping that he will abandon falsehood and return to the truth, so that he will not be confused and become enlightened, restoring himself to his existing Buddha nature. For example, the pearl Mani fell into the mud, foolish people considered it dirty, did not know it was a precious pearl, knowledge considered it a priceless pearl, fished it out of the mud, washed the dirty things, used the cleaned fragrant oil to hang it high, the light shone down on the sky and earth creating good rain.The mentality of sentient beings is the same. Even though they return to confusion and fall down the evil path, the inherent true nature of Buddha nature still does not contain permanence, is neither born nor destroyed, and has no changing appearance. Therefore, the Bodhisattva believes that any person whose karma is very serious, but does not have a single thought of abandoning that mind with the suffering of sentient beings, then has compassion and needs to be saved so that they can soon escape their suffering.

Layman Ly Vien Tinh felt the Bodhisattva's compassion and compassion for the ignorance of sentient beings, so he translated the Bodhisattva's vows into a dialogue and disseminated them, and took stories from Japan to record the stories of inspiration into 18 chapters, printed them for circulation, making all sentient beings clearly know the Bodhisattva from countless lifetimes to the present, with that compassion to bring birth to all sentient beings. from birth and death, attain Buddha nature. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

Buddha Shakyamuni once said to Universal Bodhisattva: "You should know that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva can be said to be a Bodhisattva with hundreds of thousands of millions of great supernatural power and beneficial deeds. The sentient beings in the Jambudvipa world have many karmic conditions for this Great Being. These sentient beings hear the Bodhisattva's name, see the Bodhisattva's statue, or even hear a few words in the Sutra or a verse of the sutra, and all receive great blessings and peace. happy, in the next life or in hundreds of thousands of lives, they will all be righteously reborn in a place of wealth and dignity." Buddha once said to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in Jambudvipa also has many causes and conditions. If we talk about seeing and hearing the benefits of sentient beings, it cannot be exhausted in hundreds of thousands of lifetimes. "So we get to see Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva with people in this world. There is indeed a great cause and effect, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's career of saving sentient beings is no less than that of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Buddha Shakyamuni in Dao Loi heavenly palace praised and rewarded the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Make Quan Am announce it to everyone. Therefore, we know that the two Bodhisattvas have a very deep relationship with sentient beings in this land.Most people in the world know about Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva's saving lives, but very few people understand about Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's teachings, and few people talk about Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's saving sentient beings in hell. That was such a mistake. If we finish reading this book, we will understand that: Sentient beings who want to pray for Bodhisattvas' blessings can do so right away, without having to wait until the next life. Not to mention in the Sutras it says: "Bodhisattvas are afraid of causes, sentient beings are afraid of results." Saving results is of course necessary, but saving causes is even more urgent. People who commit Ten Unwholesome Deeds in this world will die in the next life and go to hell, that is the result. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva still helps those who have gone to hell, let alone those who have not yet gone to hell, why would he not think about it?

If this Great Bodhisattva teaches in any other place, our physical eyes cannot see it, so we do not understand, but in China, there are thousands of accurate and cumulative transformations of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Right in Anhui province, Cuu Hoa Mountain, in China, there are four ashrams at four famous mountains. In Putuo Mountain in the South Sea, there is Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Ngu Dai Mountain in Son Tay, there is Bodhisattva Manjushri's Ashram. Emei Mountain in Sichuan has the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra's Ashram. Nine Flowers Mountain in Anhui has the Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha's Dharma Place. Every July, there are countless pilgrims who come to worship Mount Hoa Son. Because July 30 is the day of Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha's enlightenment. On this occasion, I would like to recount Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha's vow to establish the Bodhisattva Bodhisattva. I hope we remember this carefully, we can call Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva or Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva both.

When the Buddha passed away 1,500 years ago, in the 4th year of the Tang Dynasty, in the East there was a country called Silla, which is now Korea (Korea). In the Northeast, there was a crown prince named Kim Kieu Giac. At the age of 24, he became a monk, brought a white dog named Thien Thinh, crossed the sea to China, in Anhui province, Chi Chau prefecture, Thanh Duong district on Cuu mountain. Flowers. Remaining forever on Cuu Tu mountain, sitting in meditation for 75 years, with Son Than offering food and drink, until Duong Huyen Ton Khai Nguyen's reign on the night of July 30, the 16th year, he attained enlightenment.

Later, Man Cong also became a monk. Because I later became a monk, I had to worship my son, Master. tieu_de: Cause and Effect in the Past of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva
noi_dung:
Past Cause and Effect

By Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

Why did Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's great vow to save sentient beings exist? Once we know the Bodhisattva's past lives and causes, we can understand clearly. Bodhisattva's past life was once the son of a wealthy man, once the daughter of a Brahmin, once a King, and once a Holy Maiden of Light. All are clearly recorded in the original prayer book Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra. Now let's talk about two things, one is the son of a rich man, the other is the daughter of a Brahmin.

First of all, we talk about the very ancient past, when a Buddha named Lion Phan Tan with full Van Hanh Tathagata was born. At that time Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva was still an ordinary person, the son of a wealthy man. He saw that the Buddha's appearance was very dignified and upright, his heart was very happy, so he went to worship Buddha Tathagata and asked: Why does Buddha have such a good appearance? Buddha replied: "If you want to cultivate and have such a good appearance, you need to make a great vow, you must forever transcend all suffering of living beings to be able to achieve it." The rich man's son immediately swore before the Buddha: "From now on, if there are sentient beings in the six paths who suffer, I must find a way to save them and become a Buddha, and then I will become a Buddha. If in this world there is still the six paths of reincarnation or the three evil paths, then I will still be a Bodhisattva to save sentient beings. Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, in front of the Lion Buddha, with full effort, Van Hanh made a vow until now, not knowing that he had already done so. It's impossible to say how many great kalpas he has passed through. He has transcended countless sentient beings, so he is still a Bodhisattva and has not yet become a Buddha.

I'm talking about a very long time ago, when a Buddha named Giac Hoa Samatha Samatha Tathagata appeared in the world. At that time, there was a Brahman Saint who believed in Buddhism very much, but on the contrary, the Saint's Mother did not believe in Buddhism and even slandered the Three Jewels. Therefore, when you die, you must go to hell. The saint knew that her mother would suffer a lot after her death. Therefore, he sold all his assets to do many Buddhist works, repairing the Giac Hoa Dinh Tu Tu Tathagata pagoda and tower. One day, with sincere intention, I felt the Buddha's spirit. Suddenly I heard a voice echoing from above: "If you want to know how Mother appears, go home and recite Buddha's name and you will understand." The saint returned home, so she sat solemnly and single-mindedly recited the holy name of Lord Tathagata, who read for a day and a night, suddenly felt that she had come to a beach, the water in the sea was boiling, there were many people going in and out of there, being beaten and torn apart by demons and poisonous beasts, suffering all kinds of things, so miserable that I really didn't dare to look. The holy woman wholeheartedly recited Buddha's name, so she was not frightened at all. At that time, a Demon King came to greet him, and the Saint asked: "Where is this?". The Demon King replied: "This is the coast of hell".People in the world commit killing, stealing, adultery, lying, arguing, cursing, and committing many sins. If you die after 49 days and still have no one to pray for blessings and repent, you must go to this sea. In the East, there is a sea that is even more miserable than this sea. There is another sea in the East Sea that is even more miserable. Through three layers of karma, you will reach hell, which is even more miserable." The saint asked again: "Where is my mother now?", and told her name and date of birth and death. After examining the demon king, he replied: "When your mother first came, she had to suffer in hell, but because of a son who was filial and sought blessings, three days ago she was born in Heaven." At that time, the Saint woke up as if from a dream, knew that her mother had been transcended, and took the great vow in front of the tower of the Buddha of Self-Enlightenment King Tathagata. Vow: "In the future, all sentient beings in the three evil paths are guilty, I vow to completely save them and let them become Buddhas before I can attain Bodhi. If the sinners' hell has not ended, I swear I will not become a Buddha." Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is still a Bodhisattva to this day.

We have known the past karma of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. We should also understand that Bodhisattva in the past made a great vow to save all the suffering of sentient beings and live happily with them. All sentient beings must be saved and then become Buddhas. Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's incarnations fill the entire world. Each world incarnates into tens of thousands of millions, each body contains hundreds of thousands of millions of people, leading to the Three Jewels. Forever leaving the suffering of birth and death, arriving at a place of happiness. Therefore, every time we read the title of Bodhisattva, we often call it Namo Great Vow Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra records: Sakyamuni Buddha in Dao Loi Thien Palace rubbed Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's head, praising Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's immeasurable divine power. Compassion is beyond measure, wisdom is beyond measure, eloquence is also beyond measure, causing the Buddhas of ten thousand eons to praise them endlessly.

Buddha also kindly told the heavenly beings who were in the burning house and had not yet escaped the three worlds. Advise Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, if there are heavenly people who have even a little good root in the Buddha Dharma, they should be blessed and educated to help them grow and not let them escape. If one falls into the evil realm, one can recite a good sentence or the name of a Bodhisattva, or one verse of a Sutra from the Mahayana Sutras. One must also use divine power to save and manifest all kinds of manifestations, so as not to fall into hell, and make Heavenly beings enjoy happiness and joy. We can see Tathagata's heart to help sentient beings just like Parents love their children. Understanding the suffering of his children, he tried every way to cure them. Even though he had to suffer, he did not complain. When he was about to die, he was afraid that his children would lose their support. He tried to find relatives or friends and solemnly entrusted them to them so that they could die without repentance. We read the Ksitigarbha Sutra, and when we get to the part that the Buddha entrusted, we realize that we sentient beings are very grateful to the Buddha. tieu_de: The Merit and Benefits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva
noi_dung:
Merits and Benefits

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

Long-lasting happiness, increased blessings.

If that person dies, the replacement family member loudly recites Buddha's name, and the deceased person is absolved of all serious sins, let alone reciting Buddha's name themselves. Indicating Mechanical Response

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva often teaches and transforms sentient beings depending on their background. Thousands of thousands of careful instructions, we must clearly understand the truth of cause and effect, to avoid suffering. Because if we plant many good roots, we will reap good results, but if we plant evil roots, we will definitely get evil results. Just like when you plant pumpkins you get pumpkins, when you plant beans you get beans, deciding that the law of cause and effect is not wrong, so the Bodhisattva met a murderer and said that he would receive a short-lived retribution, thieves and robbers would receive miserable retributions, adulterers would fall as pigeons, and lovebirds would be punished. Those who are cruel and slander people will have painful retribution on their tongues, those who are angry will meet with ugly retribution, and those who are stingy will meet with the retribution of nothing. Those who are not filial to their parents will face retribution in heaven. Defaming the Three Jewels will result in deaf and mute retribution. Those who hunt and kill will meet the retribution of being reincarnated far away. Those who are arrogant and proud will meet vile retributions like those who meet sinners. Bodhisattva will tell them the retribution of all sins, if those sinners, without knowing how to repent, after receiving retribution, when they die, they will have to go to hell and suffer all kinds of suffering. Most people only know what wins and loses in the short term, do not understand the law of cause and effect, do illegal things and no longer know what the law of cause and effect is.I really don't know what tomorrow's suffering will be like? What a pitiful and unfortunate thing.

You should know that the law of retribution is divided into 3 types: The first type is present retribution, that is, doing good and evil deeds in this life, good or bad things also come in this life. The second type is retribution in this life, doing good or evil deeds, so that in the next life you will encounter blessings or misfortunes. The third type is post-retribution, in this life we ​​do good or evil deeds, we have to wait until the 3rd or 4th life, or thousands of eons or countless eons, to know the good or bad things. In short, for those who create negative karma, there is no reason why there is no retribution. In this life, people who encounter disasters, if they don't resent heaven, then blame others, and refuse to think about repaying their debts from previous lives and regret it. This type of person only sees good and evil in front of their eyes. Sometimes when they randomly do a good deed and encounter disaster, they think they should not do the good deed. Sometimes when we do evil things, we think that doing evil things is not something to worry about. Because they do not understand the law of retribution for good and evil deeds, which is not something that happens overnight but is something that has been accumulated over many lifetimes. For example, snow and ice that are 3 meters thick in winter are not formed by just one cold day. They only know how to calculate the immediate benefits.That's why people are greedy and do things that harm others, are selfish, and most people in this world don't have compassion. So why should the world not come to this level again?

In the past 10 years, there has been a battle in the Western Ocean, killing thousands of people and hundreds of millions of people starving to death. Even in China's provinces, natural disasters have killed more than millions of people. An earthquake in Japan killed many thousands of people. Let's think that in just about 10 years, it has been so disastrous. People's hearts in the past were much better than those of today, because most people believed in the principle of cause and effect. Therefore, for more than a hundred years and ten years of peace in the world, it is really nothing significant. People only know that today's people's hearts are corrupt compared to ancient people's. The current world is not as good as in the past. We can know that this is the principle of cause and effect. That is a very transparent truth. Such a world, such a family or a person. From ancient times to the present, there is no shortage of real evidence appearing. Still don't believe it? Let's look at the people in this world, some are poor, some are rich, some are miserable and some are happy. There are strong people and weak people: There are beautiful people and there are ugly people. There are wise people and there are foolish people, they are not all the same. There must be a reason there. That reason is cause and effect.There is always death in human life, but death is not the end, there is always an afterlife. That means that if there is an afterlife, then there will definitely be reincarnation. If there is reincarnation, then there will also be the morality of cause and effect, mastering it.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is extremely compassionate and only wants everyone in this world to leave suffering and be happy, so he finds every way to encourage people to understand the principle of cause and effect. Since that is the case, we take this opportunity to urgently call on everyone to clearly understand the principle of cause and effect, to know that among all sins, killing is the heaviest. We all need to be vegetarian and recite Buddha's name. If we cannot be vegetarian at the moment, it is better not to kill lives.

tieu_de: Listen to Fame and Avoid Imprisonment
noi_dung:
Listen to the name and avoid prison

During the Tang Dynasty in Ung Chau, Van district, there was a woman who often ate vegetarian food and worshiped Buddha, and had great faith. In the house, there is a wooden statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, one meter six high, very spiritual. Ly Thi had a maid, over 50 years old, who often had wrong views and did not believe in the Dharma. One day, waiting for Ly Thi to be absent from home, she took the statue and left it desolate in the yard outside the house. When Ly Thi returned, she cried and searched. Suddenly, he saw a light shining in the deserted area in front of his house. He happily went out to pick up the statue, but did not know that the Bhikkhu had done it. The next day, the Bhikkhu fainted, lost consciousness, then suddenly woke up, cried and regretted, and told herself what she had done: "When I died, I saw two mandarins riding horses, reading the official message, I committed a great sin because I destroyed and dishonored the Holy Statue." Now I have to be tied up to wait for the King's reprimand and punishment to be sent to hell. At that time, a teacher walked in. The king invited him to sit down and then respectfully asked the reason. He replied: "This person is the Servant of my sect. Even though I humiliated my statue, I cannot bear to punish her. I hope the King will show grace and grant her longevity." The king said: "I will do as you wish."At that time, I regretted it immensely, so I prayed: "Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva". Immediately, the sinners in the hall also chanted in unison, locking their arms and opening them on their own. He took my hand out of the hall. I then woke up.

After hearing this, Ly Thi respected the statue even more. Since then, people in the district have become more religious than before.

Help Father Sanh Thien

During the Tang Dynasty, in Chau Phu, there was a Grandmother of the Presiding Officer's wife who revered Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, her faith was very sincere, only her biological parents who had not yet been born believed in it. For her parents' sake, the grandmother spent money to carve a golden statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, three meters high, and sincerely worshiped him. At that time, her father had to go away because of work, and her mother was home alone. That night, a thief tried to steal clothes. Looking through the door, he saw Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva sitting solemnly. The next day, the thief disguised himself and went to the house to investigate. He saw To Thi's mother alone and did not see any Saint Statue, so he was surprised and confessed his crime. Feeling ashamed, I recounted what happened the night before.

After her father went to Phu Chau, along the way he was surrounded and killed by enemies. Suddenly, a yellow-shirted monk used his hand to block the knife, used his head to receive the spear, and was injured lying on the ground. At that time, the enemy thought he was dead and withdrew, so her Father was spared harm. He was surprised, went home and told his son about it. He had a rare feeling and went to the Buddha Hall to worship. He saw that the statue's head had a few knife marks, the yellow color faded a little, and it seemed to be bleeding. Grandmother immediately knew that it was Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha who had endured three knife blows to save her Father. Her father immediately had faith and welcomed Mother to his house, serving day and night. The three people worshiped and made offerings day and night. Her father lived until he was seventy-nine years old before passing away. Thirty-five days later, her grandmother dreamed that her father appeared, her bright body standing in the air, floating naturally, giving birth to a rare thought. She knelt down and asked, "Where do you live now?". Answered: "Living in the fourth heaven with colleagues is all about nourishing the land. Most heavenly people rely on Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for guidance. The mother lives for thirty-five years, and the child lives for twenty-five years. Her husband lives for twenty-eight years." Having finished speaking, he disappeared. From then on, everything came true for Mother and her husband as Father had said.

Since then, villagers all over Europe have been busy carving or painting images of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to worship. Everyone can enjoy the Bodhisattva's protection.

tieu_de: Reciting the Name of Ksitigarbha to Prevent Demons
noi_dung:
Reciting Ksitigarbha's Name

Free from Demons

One by one, they got sick, some vomited blood, some fainted. At that time, Tin Tu was very upset and asked the monks for a rescue method. That teacher thought for a long time and said:

When the Buddha was still alive at the foot of Pi Phu La mountain, in the wealthy Kieu De family, he was also harassed by evil spirits, in a family of about 500 people. At that time, everyone was sick and did not wake up for 10 days. At that time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva wandered to the rich man's house. At that time, he had compassion and recited the mantra to save and eliminate demons. Everyone will be at peace, you should follow that method, take refuge in Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha, and single-mindedly confess the name. Think, believe and follow, draw a picture of Bodhisattva. Since then, for 50 years, Lu Thuy district has not been bothered by ghosts anymore.

Reviving Dharma Worship

During the Tang Dynasty, in Zhongshan Mountain, in Khai Thien Pagoda, there was a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva three meters high, with a halo of four and a half meters. For a long time, it was unknown who sculpted this statue. Later, there was Mr. Dang Tong, Admiral Duong Chau. At the age of 61, he fell ill and died, his chest was still warm and he could barely breathe, so his relatives did not dare to enter the shroud. At night he suddenly woke up, cried day and night, so he asked his family to guide him to Khai Thien Tu, and asked a monk: "In the temple there is a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, three meters high, four and a half meters of halo, where is it? I want to come to worship and worship." The monks listened to the search, and after finding it, Dang Tong respected it and offered to take the statue back to worship. The monk asked: "Why?". Dang Tong replied: "When I died, I saw a fourth-rank mandarin. I was brought before a King and the King, saying: "You cannot die, serving the Dharma is your inheritance, you must live and return to the human world. He followed the King outside the city, going northeast for about five or six miles. There was an iron citadel with the door closed. Gradually, the intense firelight was seen. In prison, hundreds of thousands of sinners are suffering.

At that time, a monk entered the prison, subdued the fire, and taught the sinners. The fire gradually extinguished. Going to another iron city, in which there are eighteen levels of hell, the suffering of the sinners cannot be fully described, and saw the monk again teaching the sinners as before. After returning from the tour, that monk came out of hell and asked: "Do you know who I am?". I answered that I don't know. That monk said: "I am Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva here at Khai Thien Monastery. In the past, there was a master named Tri Tang Dharma Master, whose disciple was Dharma Master Tri Manh. In order to save the suffering of the three sentient beings, he carved my image. I obeyed, so every day for one hour I entered the eighteen levels of hell and countless small hells to teach and teach the Way. Those who had previously planted good roots and had stronger good powers immediately released their minds from suffering. In addition, those who had cut off good roots and had deep-rooted evil poisons were invincible. If you are unconscious, it is difficult to escape suffering. In this world, those with good roots are weak and can easily be saved. If once they enter the evil path, the Holy Power cannot save them, the evil will remain the same, because these unenlightened people, if they later repent, will soon be able to return to the human world thanks to the power of magic.Announce it to everyone, then admire that monk, three meters tall, the top of his head radiating a bright halo. That monk taught two verses: "If in the human world and cultivating the path, chancti can be developed if you have the mind. If you enter the evil path, your karma will be deep. There is no distinction in the mind, it cannot be saved. Just like an old person who wants to walk and stand, if he uses strength to help him, it will be easy to move forward. If he lies still without moving and does not have enough strength, then the karma that determines sentient beings will be the same." The monk finished reading two verses and then disappeared.

I lay on my hospital bed remembering this, afraid that something was wrong so I didn't dare tell anyone. Now I can see that the statue is exactly the same as what I saw with my own eyes. For that reason, I want to bring it home to worship it. The monk in the pagoda was very happy when he heard that, praised and said: "You can imitate and sculpt this statue, but you can't carry it away." And this statue is still left in Khai Thien Tu.

Changing a House into a Pagoda

During the Tang Dynasty in Gian Chau, Kim Thuy district, there was a man named Thi Lang, surnamed Dang, who has always believed in Buddhism. One day, he saw a stick with a statue of a Master carved on its head, so he took it home and stuck it on the wall. Two or three years later, he suddenly fell ill and died, but his chest was still warm, so his family suspected him but did not bury him. The next night, he woke up, crying with tears streaming down his face and said: "When I first died, two people on horseback led me into the gate of a large city. In front of the hall, I saw a large number of people chained. The King was angry and wanted to question me. At that time, a Samana, with an ugly appearance, entered the hall. The King quickly stood up respectfully, clasped his hands and knelt down, saying: "Great Saint, why have you come here?" Sa Mon said: "This Thi Lang is my servant, the King should forgive her." The king said: "Now the decision has been made, the fate is over, the real fortune is gone, it is difficult to forgive." Samana said: "Before, when I was on the Good Dharma Hall in the 33rd heaven, the Buddha told me to save the karma of sinners. Since all this time, what's more, Thi Lang hasn't committed a serious crime, so why can't he be saved?The King said: "The Great Man's Great Vow is as firm and immovable as the Diamond Mountain. I followed the instructions and let him return to the human world."

Sa Mon was very happy to take my hand and lead me down the path of life. When I was about to leave, I asked: "The teacher who saved me is my great benefactor. Please give me the Dharma name to show my gratitude?" The monk replied: "I am Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Once along the way, Thi Lang picked up a stick with my image engraved on it. Although she didn't know it yet, she brought it back and put it on the wall. For the children's joy, she carved the image on the tip of the stick. Only halfway through carving the tip of the stick, it wasn't finished yet, so the image was ugly, do you remember, Thi Lang?" After speaking, he disappeared.

Thi Lang woke up and saw that only the tip of the stick stuck on the wall remained, so she hired a worker to carve it five inches larger from sandalwood. The statue often radiates light throughout the room. Thi Lang carved another larger statue, left home to build a pagoda called Ksitigarbha, worshiping small statues inside for good men and women from near and far to admire.

tieu_de: Thanks to Ksitigarbha, one can escape from being torn apart by tigers
noi_dung:
Thanks to Ksitigarbha

Escape from Tiger Tornage

During the Tang Dynasty, in Huazhou, Hui Nhut Temple had a teacher named Phap Thuong. At the age of thirty-seven, he became a monk. When I was at home, I often went hunting. One day, I saw a light shining from a bush and was surprised, so I got off my horse and went to look, only to see a piece of rotten wood more than a meter long, so I took it home. Later, when he went hunting again, he saw that the tree was shining again and was surprised, so he picked up the log to put it on the branch. On the way back, he met a Tiger, so he rode his horse to chase him. The bowstring is broken, there is no bowstring. The Tiger returned in panic and ran away, then fell off his horse in fear. I thought to myself that I would be pounced by a Tiger, it certainly couldn't be avoided. While confused, he saw an ugly looking Master come to chase away the Tiger. I asked who are you? He said: "I am Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. The rotten piece of wood in that bush is my body. Previously, your Patriarch Sangha used this tree to build a Pagoda and create an image. Now the Pagoda has been damaged, and my statue has also rotted.

After waking up, I only heard the sound of horses neighing and could no longer see the Tiger's shadow. With great regret, I went to the place where the light shines and built a monastery, rotten wood carved a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and continued to worship with incense and lanterns, that is, Tue Nhat Tu. On February 24, Phap Thuong, who was 78 years old, told his friends: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva came to my house and said: "He was in Tu Thi Tathagata's Dharma assembly three times. During the second Dharma teaching, he was the one who attained enlightenment. Today, when he gave up his life, he was immediately born in Dao Loi." I told the Great Master: "In heaven there is a realm of five desires, very happy. If Bodhi is lost, it will be difficult to meet the Buddha. Now I vow to be reborn in the West in a world of Peace and Happiness." Bodhisattva replied: "Depending on the person's wish, if one wants to be reborn in the Pure Land, one must recite Amitābha Buddha's name for one day and one night, and concentrate on maintaining the will to be reborn." Having reached Bodhisattva, since yesterday I have been focusing on reciting Amitābha Buddha. Now that he has been reborn, he said that he clasped his hands together towards the West and passed away.

Carving Statue of Tien Than

During the Tang Dynasty, there was a young woman, the daughter of an Admiral named Tran in China. She lost her mother when she was young, and spent days and nights sadly missing her, not knowing how to see her, so she no longer had hope for life, only determined to destroy herself, to go down to the golden stream to find her. When Quan Admiral saw that situation, it felt like a knife cutting his intestines, like being rubbed with salt in his heart, but he also tried to calm him down and use comforting words:

- My child! Of all the human beings in this world, there is no one who does not want to live, but because the life span is not the same, the separation is different, the rich die early, the poor live long, because of the differences in causes, no one has ever been able to change according to their wishes. What's more, even though your mother has passed away, you still have the same mentality of knowing how to love and be sad, and how to plan for perfection. Now you take pessimism into your heart, then stop sleeping, eating, drinking, and are determined to kill yourself and leave me with yet another sadness. This will greatly damage my life in my old age. So if you miss your Mother, you should create a statue of Ksitigarbha as taught in the Buddhist scriptures, so that you can worship and pray for your Mother's soul to soon escape the cycle of suffering and be born in the Pure Land. That way, I can also repay the labor of ten months of pregnancy and three years of breastfeeding.

From then on, she felt secure, praying wholeheartedly every morning and evening for her Mother to end her suffering and be happy and free from Lac Quoc. One night, after reciting Buddhist sutras, while she was sleeping, she suddenly dreamed that a monk told her: "When I was born as a woman, my father, Thi La Thien Hien, my mother, Duyet De Loi, suffered extremely severely in hell. I made a vow of Bodhisattva to save all suffering beings, in order to dedicate that merit to save my parents for salvation. Now I feel your filial heart, so I personally went to hell, preached the Dharma, and saved her dead mother from being reborn in the Dao Loi heaven."

Tran Nu was the daughter of the Admiral. After hearing the monk say that, she was very happy. She woke up startled and told the dream story to her Father and everyone in the family. Everyone was happy and saw the robe of the statue of Ksitigarbha worshiping at home change into a dark brown color, just like in her dream when she heard the monk say that because she entered hell, if she was licked by fire and burned her robe, their belief increased to the extreme.

tieu_de: Engraved Statue of Ksitigarbha Praying for Resurrection for Mother
noi_dung:
Ksitigarbha Statue Carving

Requiem for Mother

During the Tang Dynasty, there was a young daughter of Tran Do Doc. I lost my mother when I was young and miss her day and night. Because he couldn't see his mother, he wanted to commit suicide. The Admiral comforted him: "I am also a relative. Although your mother passed away, your father is still here. Why do you want to commit suicide if you refuse to eat and drink? If you miss your mother, you should carve a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and pray to save your mother from her suffering." So he spent five hundred dollars, hired a craftsman to carve a three-meter tall statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and told Father: "Please allow it to be placed in Mother's bedroom in the past. If you want to see Mother, you can see the statue." The Admiral was moved and agreed to let me place the statue in Mother's bedroom, worshiping and worshiping her day and night. Pray to Bodhisattva to save Mother's suffering. One night I dreamed that a teacher said: "Mom is currently living in a hot hell."

When I was a girl, my father was Thi La Thien Kien and my mother's name was Duyet De Loi. After she died and suffered in Hell, she developed the Bodhi heart and vowed to relieve the suffering of sentient beings. Feeling your filial piety, I went to Hell to radiate light and preach the Dharma. Save your mother's suffering. Now born in Heaven. Tran Nu saw the monk's clothes were burned and asked why? He replied: "When entering Hell, the fire is so hot that it burns." When Tran Nu listened, she realized that her mother had escaped the accident and was very happy. From then on, he devoted his entire life to worshiping the Bodhisattva.

Don't Worry About Big Translation

During the Tang Dynasty, in Lo Chau, there was royal historian Khang Cu Thong, a most faithful person, who for many years worshiped Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and was very sincere in drawing images of Bodhisattva. Always respectful. No images have been missed, the light is bright and clear. It's all because of this faith. Accidentally, two soldiers on horseback came and chased him, he was very scared. The two military officers suddenly got off their horses and said: "We were wrong! Ksitigarbha Tan Viet. Even though he was at fault, it is difficult to blame him," and after saying that, he disappeared. When I woke up, I was even more sincere.

During the first year of Hy Tong's reign in Quang Nguyen, there was an epidemic in the country, demons were rampant, the dead piled up into mountains, and dreamed of hundreds of thousands of ghosts passing through the door of the house saying: "This house is the seventh room of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, we are servants, be careful not to enter this house." So the whole family was saved. In the year of Trung Hoa, he had to go far, so he lost his way in the snow and quickly prayed to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Suddenly there was a bird flying down the snowbank. Seeing it strangely, I chased after it until I reached the main road. When he arrived at Quang Khai, he was sick and prayed sincerely to be cured. Dreamed that the Master said: "You killed my blue bird, a crime worthy of going to hell. Now you have to pay for that karma, suffer for two days before being born in the Pure Land." After hearing this, I was happy and worshiped. The illness was cured immediately. After two days, he passed away.

tieu_de: Maintaining the Name to Solve Danger
noi_dung:
Reciting the Name to Solve Danger

During the Tang Dynasty, there was a special official named Kien Khac. He had a sincere belief in Buddhism and followed the teachings of Buddhism in life. Therefore, he was loved by the King and respected by the mandarins. Below, he was also loved by the people, who considered him a blessing. One day, he went into the temple and asked some monks: "Sir, which Buddha or Bodhisattva should a layperson like me worship?" At that time, the monks all spoke differently, in the end there was one who said: "Great officials should worship Ksitigarbha, because he obeyed the Buddha's form and vowed to save all sentient beings in the three worlds and six paths."

Kien Khac heard it, put it in his heart and asked to go to the main hall to worship Buddha. As he said goodbye to the monks and returned, he thought: Since Ksitigarbha has obeyed Buddha's teachings and vowed to save all sentient beings, why won't he save me?

He vowed to carve a statue of Ksitigarbha from that moment on, so he was determined to buy a good sandalwood tree, then choose a skilled craftsman and hire him to carve a statue that was so skillful and dignified that it moved his faith. Then he performed the ceremony to place the statue and often used incense and flowers as offerings. When walking, standing, lying, and sitting, he silently recited Ksitigarbha's name.

Around the Thien Thanh era, during the reign of King Trang Tong, the whole world was in rebellion, Kien Khac was besieged, about to see death before his eyes, but he still focused on reciting Ksitigarbha's name over and over again. At that time, the rebel army seemed to be frightened by some powerful force and dispersed, not besieging Kien Khac anymore, so he was safe and sound. When it was time for peace, he told the story to all kinds of people in that country, and everyone thought it was extremely strange.

In the reign of Truong Hung, he obeyed orders to go to a certain continent as his deputy, but when he was halfway there, he encountered unjust people surrounding him to welcome assassins. While terrified, he had no choice but to wait for them to kill him, but suddenly the perpetrators only saw a monk, not Kien Khac. They immediately regretted it immensely and asked Him to forgive their mistakes so they could repent. Then the monk happily said: "Greed, anger, and ignorance are three poisons, they cause people to wander in the three paths and six paths, suffering terrible suffering. So I advise you to try to cultivate your character, nurture loving-kindness, and take refuge in the Three Jewels, so that thanks to future peace, you will be free from the suffering of reincarnation."

After hearing these sentences briefly, they were about to bow their heads and give thanks, but the monk was nowhere to be seen, so their hearts were filled with fear, so they silently vowed to change their evil and become good, and then together returned to their country. It is thanks to the magnetic power of Ksitigarbha that Mr. Kien Khac is safe and harmless.

The next time, he missed the road and it was also dark, so he and a few other people were in the middle of the field, taking turns keeping watch. Unexpectedly, at midnight, it rained heavily, causing all the lights to go out, leaving only the statue tucked in a bun radiating light as bright as day. At that time, Mr. Kien Khac was sleeping when he suddenly heard a small voice saying: "Vietnamese men, wake up and prepare to go somewhere else immediately." He heard a few words, and thanks to the light that guided him, he quickly went to find another place to stay. After the light spread, he returned to that place to take a look, and saw the rainwater on all four sides of the mountain flowing together there, forming a deep flood. Only then did he know that Ksitigarbha saved him from death by the water god.

In Thanh Thai, he lived until he was 78 years old before passing away. As he was dying, the statue in his bun radiated light. He clasped his hands and chanted Buddha's name and peacefully passed away, following the light and soaring into the sky.

tieu_de: Chanting Ksitigarbha's Name From Military Knives
noi_dung:
Reciting Ksitigarbha's Name

Koi Binh Dao

During the Tang Dynasty in Biet Gia, Kien Khac had pure faith and served the Dharma as the Ton Chi. One day he asked a Master: "Which Bodhisattva should lay people worship?" The monks all said: We should worship Ksitigarbha to be blessed by Buddha. Kiet Khac thought to himself, if the Buddha took care of us, would he be happy for us? Immediately find sandalwood to carve a three-inch statue, wrap it in a bun, walk, stand, sit, lie down, all reciting the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. In the year of Trang Tong Thien Thanh, the world was in chaos. Kien Khac was surrounded and had difficulty escaping death. He immediately chanted Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. The Great General rode his horse and fled in terror. After the riots had calmed down, when this matter was mentioned, everyone who heard it was surprised. In the year of Truong Hung, when he went to his deputy assignment, the enemy heard that he wanted to harm him, so he waited on the side of the road, but only saw a teacher passing by, but did not see Kien Khac. Thankful for liberation, one time on the way to rest, it was raining heavily, all the lights were turned off, only the statue of Him in his bun, the light radiated as bright as day. Suddenly I heard a voice as soft as a child's: "Go now! Go now!" very surprised, thanks to the guiding light, he went to stay somewhere else. The next day, the flood was so great that the place where we had stayed last night sank to the bottom of the river.Know that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva protects you. In the second year of Thanh Thai's life, he lived until the age of 78 before passing away. While dying, the statue in its bun radiated light, so he clasped his hands and chanted Buddha's name and peacefully followed the light to the sky.

Meeting Mother Hien

During the Five Dynasties, in Vi Chau, there was a woman named Dang Thi, whose mother died early and was raised by her uncle. She missed her day and night, so she asked the teacher: "How can I meet my mother?" That teacher said: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva vows great compassion, remembers with all his heart, and will meet again." The maid called out her name day and night to pray. Then he went to see the monk again and said: "Thanks to the teacher, I want to see my mother again. Please respectfully donate clothes and print prayers." Samana then asked clearly the reason, the Lady recounted: I dreamed that I was on Master's back, then flew up into the sky to the 49th floor of Mani Bao Palace. There are many Gods there, and my mother is also there. When I came to pay my respects, my mother replied: "You should be grateful to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for bringing me here, to be able to meet you. Feeling like that, don't forget Bodhisattva's gratitude."

Fire Extinguished Live

During the Five Dynasties period in Kinh Chau, there was a man named Lie Ho, who worked as a swallow hunter. Everyone knows the language and calls himself Nhan Hung. At the age of 51, he died from bad breath. His wife threw his body in the wilderness to feed tigers and wolves. Three days later he came back to life and returned home. The wife was scared when she saw it and thought it was a ghost coming back. Hung recounted: "When I died, a chariot loaded with fire ran in front of me and was burned by fire. Suddenly a monk brought water to douse the fire. The fire went out, I felt cool inside and had hope to live. Then I saw pigs, goats, chickens, pheasants, and thousands of animals coming before the King of Hell screaming: "Give me my life. Please correct Nhan Hung's crime." The king said: "You guys are saying that, Hung is definitely an evil person. But his ancestors took refuge in Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. He was a grateful person and was exempted from disasters. Seeing this, Nhan Hung single-mindedly prayed to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name. All the birds and animals turned into human forms. The king then forgave me. From now on, I left home, calling myself Buddha No, traveling in the human world, often saying: "Hell is very miserable, diligently praying to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will be exempt from that disaster."

Change Early Death and Live Longer

During the Song Dynasty, at Khai Bao Pagoda, there was a monk named Thich Hue On who raised a pupil, but he did not know its name. At the age of 14, General Kien Chan said: "As a short-lived general, if you live another month you won't be able to feed yourself anymore." The monk heard that and sent that boy home. At that time, it was raining heavily and the road was impassable. The boy slept at a painter's house. He saw a painting of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and used his fingernails to practice drawing a picture of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva on the wall. After the rain stopped, after returning home more than a month later, the pupil returned to Khai Bao Pagoda. Hue On was very happy and said: "Today, on the occasion of Kien Chan's birthday, I invited Kien Chan to meet Dong Tu. Seeing Dong Tu's appearance, his life increased by 50 years, found it strange, I don't understand why? The student said: "I used my fingernail to draw a picture of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva on the wall. That night, a monk called me and said: "Fifty, fifty", like that three times and then disappeared.

Hue On and the Master were both surprised that this had never happened before. Later, that boy became a monk, meditated in the six levels, and was named Dharma Master Hue Tang.

Praying for Golden Blessings

During the Song Dynasty, in Tran Luu district, there was a poor young woman who worked for others to make a living, and had a hard life. She then fasted, recited the holy name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and prayed for his blessings and wealth. Self-assessment of my past karma is very heavy, I don't know if I can achieve my wish or not?

On the 24th day of the second lunar month, the 5th year of Khai Bao, she saw ants crawling all over the house, and did not dare to enter the house for fear of stepping on the ants to death. Then she saw the ants gradually turning yellow. She was scared. The neighbors saw that and were also surprised. After a day and a night, she entered the house and saw the ants disappear and saw that the carpet was full of gold, just three ounces. The young girl sold it and became rich. After that, my heart became more confident in the Bodhisattva, so I took that house and built it into a pagoda, worshiping and worshiping him. Later, there was a widowed District Lord who married that young woman and pampered him with everything.

Light Radiation Eliminates Diseases

During the Song Dynasty, the villages in Liaocheng had more than two thousand households. They had always worshiped the Dharma very much and believed strongly in Avalokiteśvara and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, especially the Avalokiteśvara Sutra and Ksitigarbha's Ten Wheels. There is an ancient pagoda with three compartments and four wings, a green roof with red carpet, on the left and right are two statues of Guan Yin and Ksitigarbha, seven and a half meters high, in the middle is a solemn statue of Amitābha Buddha, one meter high.

During the reign of King Thai Tong, the country was peaceful and prosperous. Suddenly an epidemic spread, many people died. The City Lord prayed before the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and saw a light emitting light throughout the village. Wherever the light shines, everyone will be cured. Those who have died will be resurrected. There was a Goddess who did not believe in Buddhism and died of illness. One night later, he came back to life, stayed in the monastery, prayed to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, cried and asked to become a monk. Someone asked why? The Goddess replied: "I was captured and tied by a demon. I called God to save me. I was also afraid of evil spirits. After being influenced by the Teacher, the demon left me. The Teacher said: "You are a foolish Goddess, relying on Shinto, not believing in Buddhism. I am the Bodhisattva Maha Ksitigarbha. According to the request of the Holy Master, save the lives of ignorant people, build temples in villages, protect evil spirits, I control demons, why? Demons create their own karma." The Goddess narrated the words of the Teacher, and said to herself: "Now I see this incident and am resurrected. From now on, I have reformed my ways, so I want to become a monk." Everyone happily let the Goddess become a Nun.

Praying for Teething

During the Song Dynasty, in Thien Phuc Pagoda, in the northeast corner, there was a statue of Ksitigarbha, one meter six meters high, it is unknown who carved it and when. All I know is that many people say that the statue is very magical, and those who come to sleep or pray for something are very successful. At that time, a layperson, about thirty-seven years old, but without any teeth, came to the statue, not eating and praying gently all over his body. In the middle of the night, I dreamed that the statue came to touch its head, and soon it grew 38 teeth. Everyone heard and saw such a strange thing, so they imitated the drawing of Ksitigarbha's image and set up an altar to worship, and they were all inspired. A lot of people know this story.

Your Daughter

During the Song Dynasty, in Hai Lang district, there was a group of children playing on the beach, playing with drawings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva on the sand. Suddenly, they heard thunder and lightning, and everyone ran away in fear. At that time, a Master came to the rescue. Those who fall are lifted up, those who cry are comforted. At that time, a painter's child was so frightened that he ran into the sea. The Master rescued him and brought him to shore, giving him all kinds of food and a pearl shaped like glass and as big as a lotus seed. The father took it home and carved it into a Saint statue. The child grows up healthy and very wealthy.

Bodhisattva Incarnation

During the Song Dynasty, there was a monk named Tri Huu, a native of West India, who came to China in the year Thien Phuc, staying at Thanh Thai Temple. In the sutra, there is an image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and in the Sutra of the Vow of Merits, in Sanskrit, in the middle circle there is a statue and image of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, wearing a crown and holding a treasure in his hand. On the right and left sides there are 10 Saint images. The five on the left are: Qin Quang Vuong, So Giang Vuong, Song De Vuong, Ngu Quan Vuong and Diem La Vuong. On the right, there are five people: 1. Kha Thanh Vuong, 2. Thai Son Vuong, 3. Equal Equality King, 4. Do Thi Vuong, and Five Paths Chakravartin King. Everyone has their own fate, fortune, Phu Quan, Dien Quan, etc. They say to themselves: "In the past, in Western India, there was a Bodhisattva of Compassion who saved the world and made a great vow. In order to save the three disciples and suffer on behalf of sentient beings, he drew a picture of Ksitigarbha. He came to the Thap Kings City and announced: "Today I vow to save the sufferings of the three disciples, so I should help." The Ten Kings clasped their hands in reverence and promised, and said before the image: "All sentient beings belong to the Great Saint, depending on your needs. Tao. We are just assistants." At that time, the statue smiled and said: "How wonderful! How good! The sins of sentient beings will soon be alleviated."Immediately release light to illuminate the suffering of the three disciples. Sentient beings are enlightened, all suffering is relieved. That's destiny. I met a monster in Luu Sa and prayed to Bodhisattva. Therefore, you should hold a staff to chase and fight. Again in the night of heavy rain, miserable because there was no light, no direction, no distinction between Southeast and Northwest, ferocious beasts roared. Both people and horses lost their way, the statue radiated light like day, the beasts ran away, and the path was clear. When crossing the river, we encounter big waves. The wind and waves arise without knowing how deep or shallow they are. The water flows weakly, and trees and leaves cannot float, let alone boats. Then when I chanted the Holy Statue, I saw a Teacher with two pupils, one hand holding a phan, the other holding an oar. The Master holds the talisman in his hand. So we crossed the shore, and when we reached the eastern shore, we said goodbye. Giving the monk a talisman, this is the Earthly Way.

Drawing in a style, letting everyone follow, is very unique. Three years later, no one knows where Tri Huu and the statue are. Everyone thought they were back in India. Everyone believes that Tri Huu is the reincarnation of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

Bodhisattva's Four Great Vows

Infinite sentient beings vow to save

Endless afflictions and broken vows

The practice of immeasurable vows to learn

Buddha's unsurpassed vow to fulfill.

Translation:

Beings have no number

Vow to universal salvation

Afflictions are endless

All vows are ended

Unspeakable Dharma methods

Vow to practice and study

Buddhism is nothing more

The vow is fulfilled.

tieu_de: Chanting the Ksitigarbha Sutra to Save a Mother Who Was Sick of a Perforation (This story is not in the translation)
noi_dung:
Chanting the Ksitigarbha Sutra to Save Mother

Healing Perforation

(This story is not in the translation)

Once upon a time there was a female teacher named Cao Tong Thanh, nicknamed Tuyet Tai, born in Ngo district, China. Lady Phan, her mother, is over seventy years old, and is always sick. Sometimes she takes all kinds of medicine but doesn't feel strong. In the spring of the Year of the Dragon, her illness became more serious, her whole body was punctured. The doctor said it was a case of "Severe Qi Deficiency", waiting until the water stagnant in the flesh fibers had completely dissolved before she died. There was no cure.

At that time, Tuyet Tai was teaching in Than Gian and could visit once a month. She saw that Mother's condition had reached the point of death, her skin was swollen and shiny, she felt like she wanted to sob, and when she heard Mother screaming and moaning endlessly, her heart was filled with sadness. She didn't know what to do, so she went to tell her story to a close friend, and asked if she knew how to ask for help. Because he knew early in his belief in Buddhism and often saw many miracles, he advised Tuyet Tai to recite the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra and pray for her mother. She immediately returned home and vowed to become a vegetarian and receive thirty volumes of the Ksitigarbha Sutra.

On May 27, she had just completed her chanting. When the sun had just passed, she saw her mother develop vaginal discharge and urinate non-stop, all night until morning. Everyone in the family was frightened, afraid that she would not survive. Sure enough, the next day, the holes in her body all collapsed and her skin was no longer as smooth as before. Then gradually she was able to eat and drink and became healthy as usual. Ms. Tuyet Tai was very happy and knew it was thanks to Ksitigarbha's inspiration that this happened. So she believed in Buddhism even more, kept eating vegetarian food and chanting sutras until her mother passed away.

At that time, she worried about the difficult funeral and gradually paid back her filial piety. After that, she submitted her resignation as a teacher and went to the mountains to cultivate her career. As for the people in that district, seeing such inspiration, they all believed in Buddhism very much.

Text After Editing

tieu_de: Chanting the Sutra to Meet Mother
noi_dung:
Chanting the Sutra to Meet Mother

Wu Khe Bi layperson from Jiangsu province, May 17, 1928. His mother passed away. After the second loss, he met layperson Van Thieu and advised him to recite the Ksitigarbha Prayer Sutra. Starting from that day, he lit incense and recited prayers once a day, until the last day of his retreat. A month later, the lay person was sleeping soundly at night and suddenly remembered: "If anyone wants to meet, he will surely meet: So he recited the names of Amitābha Buddha and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Thanks to the power of the gods, he was able to reach Mother. Suddenly, as if there was a hand pushing him on the back of his head, telling him to go in the flying direction. Through the wall without any obstacle, his eyes were half open, all four sides could see dimly, he went a very long way to reach a place.

Suddenly someone behind said: "Already here?" The layman said: "Still haven't seen anything, what should we do now?" The layman looked straight and saw a bush, so he knelt down and asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to let him know that his Mother was near and far. Suddenly there was a sound from above, someone answered, but they haven't been found yet. So he asked the person who was going with him, what was his answer? The person who went there with him replied that he would not back down. The layperson recites: Even though he has not regressed, it means he has been born in the West. The person who answered this was Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Then he bowed and said: "Please Bodhisattva, show great compassion so that I can see Mother." The person walking together said: "Look ahead." The layman raised his head to look forward and saw that the Dinh Dai pavilion was very solemn. On the left there is a cliff, above there is a building. The lay mother came to the window to look out, smiling and waving. The layperson called for Mother, and suddenly saw her standing in the hallway, wearing a light yellow shirt, muttering towards the layperson, but did not hear anything. The layman asked Mother to say it again. Mom said again: The layperson's name is also here and wants to ask Mom if she feels pain when she is about to die?The lay mother turned her back to another place, then loudly said: "Please take care of your body." In a moment, the Mother went up a high mountain and then disappeared. The layman clasped his hands and raised his face to the sky to thank the Bodhisattva. At that moment, he woke up. Nhiep Van Dai listened to the layman recount the situation in the dream and recorded it. Layman Ngo was a philosophy scholar at an American university. After returning home, he accepted the position of Standing Editor-in-Chief of An Thu Quan, and later became principal of To Chau High School. In the past 10 years, lay people have abandoned all positions. Now it is revising the Dan Quoc Dai Tripitaka. The spirit of asceticism and sacrifice of lay people manifests a great deal of understanding in Buddhism.

Deaf Hearing Buddha's Voice

Quan Thiet Thieu was a reformist leader

about Oriental medicine. After graduating from Nam Duong Cong Hoc School, he worked as an excellent professor, taught English, then worked as an Editor at Standing Office Library, studied medicine, especially Trung Canh's Thuong Han Luan, which was very clear and very effective in treating diseases. Because I read many of his articles, I often wrote letters to inform and visit each other, so we became good friends. He often advised people to study Buddhism, although he did not consider it mandatory to write letters to argue with each other.

In the fall of the 23rd year (1934), he sent the book Pure Land Saint Hien Luc as a gift, and then sent a reply saying: I just read the first page and still don't believe it, but after thinking about it myself, I don't believe it even more. It's because I'm stubborn, so just try to believe it. Then continued reading page two, feeling hesitant. After reading the Ksitigarbha Prayer Sutra sent by him within ten days, there was no longer any doubt.

In the 9th lunar month, which is the birth date of Avalokiteshvara, at four o'clock in the morning, I suddenly heard the sound of the funeral, then heard the sound of reciting the Buddha's name, every sentence was very clear. Quan Thiet Thieu has been deaf for more than ten years. Even if there is a loud voice in his ear, he cannot hear anything. Now I can hear the sound of reciting the Buddha's name continuously for more than ten sentences, a wonderful sound. Never heard it in my life. At first I suspected that the lady was praying, but at that time she was still lying next to me and had not yet woken up, very surprised and trembling. At four o'clock the next morning, I heard the sound of Buddha's name again like the day before. That afternoon, while sitting downstairs, I heard the same chanting as before. First, I heard the sound of the opening ceremony, then I heard the sound of reciting Buddha's name. One day I ate crab. The next morning, I didn't hear the sound of Buddha's name anymore. Then he volunteered: "I swear from now on I will never eat crab again." Then recite Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva seven times. Next, Khanh arose again, followed by the sound of reciting the Buddha's name.

From then on, for about half a year, every day he heard the sound of Buddha's name. At first, I thought it was a brain disease, but why couldn't I hear other voices? Only then did I know that it was the Premonition of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, guiding me to recite the Buddha's name. On March 24, he sent someone with two hundred silver to print the Ksitigarbha sutra, telling him to tell this story to repay Buddha's favor. At that time, I sent letters many times recounting that strange story.

In June of Summer, he passed away. The wife and children recounted the situation before their death and recorded it as follows:

He knew about three or four days in advance that he was about to leave, gave him very clear instructions, and ordered his family not to cry. Everyone recited Buddhist scriptures together. The morning before his death, he raised his head and looked around, asking his family members: "Have you seen my ledger?" The servant asked: "What is written in the notebook?" He raised his head again, looked around slowly and said: "There is a lot written, but the words are not clear" and continued, "I am going to a good land, don't be sad". He continued: "I know the past and the future." When his family asked him to speak roughly, he replied: "It's impossible to say everything! You must take care of reciting Buddha's name." After saying that, he continued to mutter the Buddha's name to himself non-stop. Before he died, he could no longer speak, but his lips still moved to recite Buddha's name, then went to the Western Pure Land.

Based on the time he was born, he held the position of Editor in the Novel Magazine at the Standing Committee of An Quan. In the articles he wrote, there were often words that slandered Buddhism, and when he spoke, he often criticized and mocked Buddha. Especially when his wife recited Buddha's name for more than ten years, he told his friends: "She wants to live in the West, I will live in the East." He considered himself an intellectual and often ridiculed Buddhists as superstitious people. But he had enough good roots, and in the writings there were many things that were suitable for him. In the end, he turned to Buddhism and enjoyed real benefits. Be guided by compassionate Bodhisattva. With deaf ears every day, hearing the Buddha's name so that you can follow the method of reciting the Buddha's name for rebirth, the method cannot help but arouse faith in Buddha. Besides, for the past few months I've been constantly hearing voices, so I can't help but feel that ghosts, gods and Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are often lurking around me, causing panic. Therefore, he sincerely repented and his bad karma gradually disappeared. He recorded it in the ledger, meaning his whole life's good and bad karma. At first, he did not let anyone know about that notebook. His thoughts moved him, so he wrote it down himself.That is my mind, heaven or hell are expressed by my heart. Sin or punishment, Pure Land or Ultimate Bliss, everything is felt by our karma. In that book, it is written that in the moment of survival, that is the good and evil of one's life manifested. Ordinary people are like that, they often get mentally confused, unable to control themselves, as well as coughing and having asthma. We just try to calm down and act as if nothing happened, which is also impossible. There are only people who cultivate pure karma and die in peace and relaxation. Even though I have a serious illness, I don't feel any pain at this time, so I can leisurely recite Buddha's name without being hindered by worldly karma.

Readers should not think that clearly reciting Buddha's name when about to die is easy or normal and take it lightly. The Amitabha Sutra says: "It is impossible to go to the Buddha's Kingdom without good roots and good causes." Mr. Thiet Thieu is an honest man who dares to courageously narrate his work to save humanity. That is your pure karma achievement.

living beings, With the 32 Reflections Body, liberate all sentient beings. Thien Thu Thien Nhan saves all suffering. Truong Thi's sister-in-law's name is Tho Than, her dharma name is Thang Tho, Tran Boi Ngoc, from Tran Giang district, Fujian. Born into an honest family, intelligent from a young age, when he grew up he read Confucian books. When she was at home, she was very filial to her parents. When she was old enough, she returned to Giang Ha to be the daughter-in-law of Chief Ton Du Duong Cong. After 49 days of marriage, her husband died, and she vowed to worship him. Her mother-in-law was seriously ill and the medicine was ineffective. She cut up meat to make medicine. Because of her filial piety, she touched the heavens, and her mother-in-law's life was extended by 3 years. Relatives from both sides of the family praised him. In the family, from her sister-in-law, grandchildren, to the maid and neighbors all praised Truong Thi's virtue. There were people who came to ask for help when they were hungry or sick and Truong Thi wholeheartedly helped them, never giving up. Life is very frugal, eating, drinking and dressing are very simple.

In May of the 30th year of the Republic of China (1941), Dharma Master Venerable Hoang Nhat propagated the Dharma. My sister-in-law invited me to go see the Dharma Master with her, to take refuge in the Three Jewels and fast in February, June and September. I also haven't gone to my husband's house because of work. Her husband died, so she spent time spending time with her beloved sister-in-law for more than ten years. One night, I looked at Sister-in-law's appearance, as close as sisters. Suddenly she got breast cancer, which got worse every day. A few months later, on June 2, Tuat time, she passed away. Let go of your body and be reborn in the West. After death, his father remained. Since before, I have only studied on my own without any monks giving me any guidance. What a pity. When Sister-in-law was sick, she still persisted in eating long-lasting fruit, putting aside all thoughts, wholeheartedly reciting Buddha's name to seek birth in the West. While she was seriously ill, the whole family was more than ten people big and small, everyone was vegetarian. Several dozen people took turns day and night to recite the Buddha's Recitation Sutra without interruption. Her sister-in-law's brother, Chan Dinh, a lay person, often came to advise and comfort her, so her sister-in-law became even more wise.

When she was dying, Ton Thua Kinh's nine-year-old grandson, under the light of an electric light, suddenly screamed loudly, his face pale. People patted and asked why? Thua Kinh replied: "Behind you, there is a person with the appearance of a Buddha, tall, wearing a hat with many corners, wearing a shirt with many patches, holding a staff in his hand, leading you." Because at that time there was a picture of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva hanging in the house, everyone thought that Thinh Duc sensed the arrival, so Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva came to take her to give birth in the West, there was no longer any doubt.

The sister-in-law had a special trip to a Western scenic spot, so all funeral rituals followed Buddhist rituals. Five days later, he was cremated in Vu Son. Cremated in less than two hours, the clean white ashes were taken out, put in a jar, and are now deposited in Thanh Nguyen mountain, Di Da cave, waiting for a day to be chosen to build a memorial tower. I think of all her honorable actions when she was born. Although her culture is poor, I would like to note a few points about her virtues.

In terms of her appearance, Thanh Nhan Truong Nu Si is my relative. I often hear that she is a dignified and virtuous person. She passed away one morning thanks to the in-laws of layperson Chan Dinh who came to visit and recite Buddha's name to dedicate her life. I heard that Ton Thua Kinh's nephew saw the image of the Holy Statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva appear. When I asked Thua Kinh carefully, it was exactly what everyone said. That child is 9 years old, has been in school for a few years, is very smart, is a modern child, and has never believed in Buddhism. Suddenly recounting seeing the Buddha statue with his own eyes, that was enough to know that he was influenced by Thinh Duc of the Female Scholar, without any doubt. That is the transformation of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the Dharma for life. People's sins are so deep and heavy that it is very difficult to hear the name of a Buddha or a Bodhisattva, let alone see a statue of a Bodhisattva?

She returned to her husband's house to take care of her uncle and aunt. The neighbors praised her and made her one of the best women. The entire Hoang family and sister-in-law all have noble temperament, which is very rare. In the future, Boi Ngoc Maitreya passes away and is reborn in the West, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will surely come to guide her.

Before, I felt the Bodhisattva of Compassion bless me, it was unbelievable. That was recorded by Khe Vien But. It's been fifteen years since I believed in Buddha. Because he was in the military ranks and had little time to practice, the Ksitigarbha Sutra had not been read. In the 32nd year of the Republic of China (1943), I served in Guangdong Hung, the Ninh Phong Air Command headquarters. Among my colleagues were two men named Tran who liked to shoot birds in flight. I often advise and take the opportunity to praise the Buddha Dharma, and praise all the divine power and merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. The relatives of two people named Tran and one named Hua were influenced by the Buddha's teachings and all set up altars to worship and praise the Holy Name of Bodhisattva. The Hua family's faith is very solid, very diligent and respectful.

In the fall of that year, due to illness, I resigned and returned to my hometown. One day, at home, I suddenly opened the Ksitigarbha Sutra to read. Just a few pages in, I felt a fragrance emanating from the Sutra. Not long after, I smelled a subtle fragrance that filled the house and never dissipated. At that time, I was sick and had not recovered, because my poor family did not have enough money to buy medicine for treatment. A few days later, there was an emergency alarm. I quickly ran to the shelter. As soon as I left the door, enemy planes came and bombed heavily. I am a sick person, so scared that I fainted, lying on the ground like someone lost in the wind. At that time, everyone in the family had run into the air defense bunker, so no one knew anything. I fell asleep at 3pm and didn't wake up until 7pm, four hours. What's even more strange is that two days later, my illness suddenly cured completely. That is also thanks to the power of Buddha's Compassion. Now, thanks to the grace of Buddha and Bodhisattva, this story should be recorded to remember forever.
